title: DeepSEA Multi-Task Deep CNN Predicts Chromatin and Functional Impacts of Noncoding Human Genome Variants
whyItMatters: Published in Nature Methods, DeepSEA predicted 919 chromatin and transcription-factor profiles directly from 1-kb DNA windows—prioritizing pathogenic noncoding mutations across the 98% non-protein-coding human genome.
summary: Published in Nature Methods on August 24, 2015, Jian Zhou and Olga G. Troyanskaya at Princeton University created DeepSEA, a deep multi-task convolutional neural network trained jointly on 919 ENCODE and Roadmap Epigenomics functional profiles (DNase hypersensitivity, histone marks, and transcription-factor binding) across 1,000-bp genomic windows. Predicting chromatin effects purely from raw DNA sequence at single-nucleotide resolution, DeepSEA prioritized eQTLs and disease-associated noncoding variants far more accurately than evolutionary conservation alone—establishing the direct architectural lineage leading to Enformer and AlphaGenome.
technicalHighlights: Jointly predicted 919 cell-type-specific chromatin, histone, and transcription-factor profiles directly from 1-kb DNA sequences.
Unlocked single-nucleotide variant-effect prioritization across the 98% noncoding human genome without prior functional annotations.
Direct conceptual and architectural ancestor of ExPecto, Enformer, and DeepMind’s AlphaGenome.
caveats: Receptive field was limited to 1-kb local sequence context, missing distal enhancers tens to hundreds of kilobases away.

scoreRationale.foundational: First deep multi-task chromatin-profile sequence model enabling de novo functional interpretation of noncoding human mutations.
scoreRationale.ripple: Directly shaped the next decade of regulatory-genomics AI culminating in Enformer and AlphaGenome.
scoreRationale.verification: Peer-reviewed in Nature Methods (Vol. 12, pp. 931–934) and validated on eQTL and HGMD disease-mutation cohorts.
scoreRationale.velocity: Evaluated functional impacts of millions of candidate noncoding variants in seconds.
